pharm: Synthetic progestogen that binds progesterone receptors, suppresses gonadotropins, thickens cervical mucus, and transforms the endometrium.
quick: POP contraception: 0.35 mg once daily; menstrual disorders: 5 mg 2-3 times daily
Take at the same time each day; food not required
Progestin-only pills compatible; small amounts in milk
Use with caution; no specific adjustment established
Contraindicated in acute liver disease or liver tumors
BP, bleeding pattern, breast exam, signs of thrombosis
summary: Norethisterone (US name norethindrone) is a synthetic progestin. The progestin-only oral contraceptive (norethindrone 0.35 mg) is taken continuously at the same time each day to prevent pregnancy. Higher-dose norethisterone (commonly 5 mg) is used for menstrual disorders such as menorrhagia, dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, and delaying menstruation. It must not be used in pregnancy or active liver disease.
indications: Primary and secondary amenorrhea, irregular menstruation

dosage.d: 0.35 mg once daily, continuously, at the same time each day
dosage.n: No pill-free interval; a backup method is needed if a dose is >3 hours late

dosage.d: 5 mg two to three times daily for ~10 days (regimen varies)
dosage.n: Withdrawal bleed follows discontinuation; per local protocol/BNF

dosage.d: 5 mg daily, may increase up to 15-20 mg/day
dosage.n: Continued for several months per protocol

dosage.d: 5 mg three times daily, started ~3 days before expected period
dosage.n: Continue until postponement no longer required; bleeding occurs 2-3 days after stopping

admin: Take the progestin-only pill at the same time every day without a break between packs
If a contraceptive pill is more than 3 hours late, use additional contraception for 48 hours
For menstrual indications, follow the prescribed start day and course duration
Use a non-hormonal backup if vomiting/severe diarrhea occurs within hours of a dose
moa: Norethisterone binds progesterone receptors to produce progestational effects. Contraceptive efficacy derives mainly from thickening cervical mucus (impeding sperm), endometrial changes hostile to implantation, and partial suppression of the LH surge and ovulation. In menstrual disorders it stabilizes and then induces orderly withdrawal of the endometrium.

absolute: Benign or malignant liver tumors; acute liver disease
relative: History of venous thromboembolism or thrombophilia

preg: Contraindicated in known or suspected pregnancy. Discontinue if pregnancy occurs; progestins are not indicated to support pregnancy in this context.
lact: Progestin-only pills are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; small amounts pass into milk without significant effect on milk supply or the infant. Estrogen-free, so preferred over combined pills during lactation.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment established; use with caution and monitor for fluid retention.
hepatic: Metabolized by the liver; contraindicated in acute liver disease and liver tumors. Avoid in significant hepatic impairment.

major: Hepatic enzyme inducers (rifampin/rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St John's wort): reduced contraceptive efficacy
Certain HIV/HCV protease inhibitors and some antiretrovirals (altered progestin levels)
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (may raise progestin levels)
Lamotrigine (combined products lower lamotrigine; progestin-only less affected)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; consistency of timing is key for contraception.
interactions.diagnostics: May alter sex-hormone-binding globulin, lipid, and coagulation test results.

emergency: Signs of VTE/PE (leg swelling, chest pain, breathlessness)

monitoring: Pregnancy status if menses absent on POP
counsel: Take the contraceptive pill at the same time every day with no break
If a pill is more than 3 hours late, use backup contraception for 48 hours
Irregular bleeding/spotting is common, especially at first
Seek urgent care for leg pain/swelling, chest pain, breathlessness, or severe abdominal pain
Tell your clinician about all medicines, including epilepsy and TB drugs
pk: Endometrial effects within days; contraceptive cover builds over 48 hours
pearls: Progestin-only pill must be taken at the same time daily; the late-dose window is only 3 hours
Estrogen-free, making it suitable during breastfeeding and where estrogen is contraindicated
High-dose norethisterone is widely used to delay menstruation and treat menorrhagia
Enzyme-inducing drugs can reduce contraceptive efficacy
missed: Contraceptive use: if more than 3 hours late, take the pill as soon as remembered, continue the next at the usual time, and use additional contraception for 48 hours. For menstrual-disorder dosing, take when remembered and resume the schedule.
overdose: Overdose is not expected to cause serious harm; nausea, vomiting, and withdrawal bleeding in women may occur. No specific antidote; manage symptomatically.
